title: nVent Breaks Ground on Kansas Manufacturing Expansion to Support Growing Demand for Engineered Building Solutions
body_markdown:
NEWS ARTICLE


nVent Breaks Ground on Kansas Manufacturing Expansion to Support Growing Demand for Engineered Building Solutions


*58,000-square-foot expansion will increase production capacity, create skilled manufacturing jobs, and strengthen support for critical electrification infrastructure.*


nVent recently celebrated the groundbreaking of a significant expansion at its Pittsburg, Kansas manufacturing facility, reinforcing the company's continued investment in growth, innovation, and the accelerating global demand for electrification infrastructure.


More than 100 employees, customers, community leaders, trade partners, and local stakeholders gathered on August 21 to mark the start of construction on a 58,000-square-foot expansion of the site, which manufactures nVent's Engineered Building Solutions. The investment will increase manufacturing capacity, create new skilled jobs, and enhance nVent's ability to deliver critical infrastructure solutions for customers across the power, utilities, industrial, energy, and data center markets.


"As electrification continues to transform industries around the world, our customers need scalable, reliable infrastructure solutions delivered with speed and quality," said Tom Atkinson, who leads nVent's Engineered Building Solutions business. "This expansion reflects nVent's continued investment in our people, our manufacturing capabilities, and our ability to help customers connect and protect critical systems that power modern life."


## Expanding Capacity for Growing Infrastructure Demand


The Pittsburg expansion is designed to support increased production of nVent's Engineered Building Solutions, including prefabricated electrical houses, or e- houses, that serve as critical power-distribution and control centers. These engineered structures are used in applications ranging from utility substations and renewable energy installations to industrial facilities, data centers, transportation systems, and other mission-critical infrastructure projects.


Factory-built and tested before arriving on site, e-houses help customers accelerate project schedules, reduce construction complexity, improve safety, and increase reliability. As industries invest in grid modernization, renewable energy, digitalization, and electrification, demand for these integrated solutions continues to grow.
